newsitem.title: PERU: Peru sees $240 mln loan from LatAm Reserve Fund.
newsitem.headline: Peru sees $240 mln loan from LatAm Reserve Fund.

text.p: Peru's Economy and Finance Minister Jorge Camet told Congress Friday the government had received a loan offer from the Latin American Reserve Fund worth $240 million.
"Yesterday I spoke with the president of the Latin American Reserve Fund and he offered me a $240 million loan for Peru," Camet said.
The Latin American Reserve Fund is an entity of the region's central banks created to aid governments with their current account spending.
Camet did not specify what the loan would be used for.

But earlier in the year, the minister said the reserve fund would form part of a group of creditors loaning money to Peru to allow the government to finance its Brady Plan which will restructure the bulk of its commercial debt.
Last week, the Inter-American Development bank said it approved a $235.5 million loan to Peru as part of the financing package to help the government start up its Brady Plan.
Camet has said the cost of the Brady start-up would also be financed by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and Japan's Eximbank.
Earlier this month, the Peruvian government signed a Brady bond accord with its creditors containing the final details of the restructuring of $4.4 billion of principal and interest.

Officials have said 180 commercial creditors, accounting for 99 percent of the debt included in the agreement, had selected one or more of the options available in the plan which include discount bonds, par bonds, front-loaded interest rate bonds (Flirbs) and debt buyback.

The Brady restructuring accord will reduce the total commercial debt to around $5 billion, according to the government. A ministry official, who asked not to be named, said 30 percent of this would be covered by a debt buyback.
The government hopes to formally close the Brady Plan by the end of January.
